meta.title: HDRcue
meta.description: HDRcue turns HDR on while your movie player or game is open, and puts the display back when it closes.
hero.title: HDR when you need it, back to normal when you're done
hero.text: HDRcue switches HDR on or off for the apps you choose. Open your movie player and the display turns HDR on. Close it and the display goes back to how it was.
hero.note: Free for Windows 10 and 11 · Pro upgrade with a 14-day free trial
steps.title: How it works
steps.1.title: Pick an app
steps.1.text: Choose from the apps you have open, or browse for any .exe file.
steps.2.title: Pick a display
steps.2.text: Click the display on a map laid out like your desk, and choose HDR on or off.
steps.3.title: Use the app as usual
steps.3.text: HDRcue changes the display when the app opens and puts it back when it closes.
guide.title: Guide
guide.rules.title: The rules page
guide.rules.text: Right now shows what each display is doing. Below it, your rules are listed under Apps and Games. Each card shows when the rule runs, the display and what changes, with its status, a switch to turn the rule off, and a menu to edit or delete it.
guide.rules.status: Active: the app is open and its rule is in effect.
Waiting: the rule is ready and the app is not open.
Off: you switched the rule off. It stays saved.
Paused: every rule is paused from the tray or the window.
Needs Pro: the rule uses an option marked PRO and Pro isn't on. It stays saved and runs again once Pro is on.
Display not connected: the rule starts working again once that display is back.
guide.add.title: Adding an app
guide.add.text: Select Add app, pick the app, then the display and what HDR should do. Each app has one rule, so picking an app that already has one opens that rule instead.
guide.tray.title: The tray icon
guide.tray.text: Click the icon to see each display, switch HDR by hand, pause every rule, or open HDRcue. Right-click it for a short menu with Restore all displays now and Exit.
guide.restore.title: Putting displays back
guide.restore.text: HDRcue remembers how each display was before it changed it. When the app closes, the display goes back to that, so HDR you turned on yourself stays on. If the PC restarts or HDRcue closes unexpectedly, the displays are put back the next time it starts.
guide.settings.title: Settings
guide.settings.text: Start with Windows, animations, accent color and language. You can also restore every display from here, and select See Pro to try or buy Pro.
help.title: Help

help.items.question: The HDR choice is greyed out
help.items.answer: Windows reports that this display doesn't support HDR. Check Settings > System > Display > HDR in Windows. If HDR can't be turned on there, HDRcue can't turn it on either.

help.items.question: My app isn't in the list
help.items.answer: The first tab shows apps with a window open. Open the app first, look in the All apps tab, or use Browse for .exe.

help.items.question: A display stayed in HDR or SDR
help.items.answer: Open HDRcue and choose Restore all displays now in Settings, or from the tray menu.

help.items.question: HDR keeps switching on and off
help.items.answer: Another program may be switching HDR for the same app. Close it, or turn off its rule for that app.

help.items.question: How do I try Pro?
help.items.answer: Open HDRcue, go to Settings and select See Pro, then Try free for 14 days. The trial can be used once and the days count from when you start it. Afterwards the app goes back to the free version and your rules stay saved.

help.items.question: Uninstalling
help.items.answer: Uninstall HDRcue from Start or Settings > Apps. Its settings are removed with it.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.text: Found a problem or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub. English or Thai are both fine.
pro.title: HDRcue Pro
pro.text: HDRcue is free. Pro is an optional upgrade you buy once, inside the app, through the Microsoft Store. There's no subscription.

pro.features.title: HDR that follows the file
pro.features.text: In mpv and mpv.net, HDR films turn HDR on and everything else stays in SDR.

pro.features.title: A refresh rate that fits the film
pro.features.text: The display switches to a rate that fits the film's frame rate, such as 144 Hz for a 24 fps film, so pans don't stutter.

pro.features.title: Couch mode
pro.features.text: Make a TV the main display and turn the other displays off while an app is open. They come back when it closes.

pro.features.title: Full screen only
pro.features.text: A rule runs only while the game is full screen, so HDR stays off in its launcher.

pro.features.title: HDR follows the app
pro.features.text: Move the app to another display and HDR moves with it.

pro.features.title: Brightness and color profile per app
pro.features.text: Set the brightness of DDC/CI displays and pick a color profile for each app. Color profiles need Windows 11.

pro.features.title: More conditions
pro.features.text: Run a rule only while the PC is plugged in, at certain times of day, while a display is connected, or while the window is on a chosen display.

pro.features.title: Set up your games
pro.features.text: Finds the games installed from Steam, Xbox and Epic and sets them up at once.

pro.trial: Try it free for 14 days: open HDRcue, go to Settings and select See Pro. No card needed. When the trial ends, the app goes back to the free version and your rules stay. If you tried Pro in an earlier version, you get 7 more days once.
pro.free: Always free: HDR on or off per display for each app, resolution and refresh rate, while open or while in front, putting displays back afterwards and after a crash, the tray panel, an HDR shortcut, silent mode, sound output (experimental) and importing settings from AutoActions.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: HDRcue works entirely on your PC.
privacy.reads.title: What HDRcue reads
privacy.reads: Running apps: which programs are running and where their executable files are, to know when an app with a rule opens or closes. It does not read what those apps show or contain.
Displays: each display's name, size, refresh rate and HDR state, to show them and to switch HDR.
Installed apps: the apps in your Start menu, listed when you add a rule, and your Steam, Xbox and Epic game libraries when you open the games page.
Playback in mpv: when you turn on HDR by file, the format and frame rate of the video mpv is playing, read through mpv's own connection on your PC.
Sound outputs, display brightness and color profiles, and whether the PC is plugged in, for the rules that use them.
privacy.stores.title: What HDRcue stores
privacy.stores: Your rules and settings, the display state it needs to put your displays back, when you started the Pro trial, and a small log of errors. These are files in HDRcue's own folder on your PC, plus one value in the Windows registry for your user account that keeps a second copy of the trial dates. When HDRcue is installed from the Microsoft Store, that value is in the app's own private part of the registry. Uninstalling the app removes all of them.
privacy.sends.title: What HDRcue sends
privacy.sends: Nothing to us or anyone else. HDRcue has no telemetry and no account. The only connection it makes is to the Microsoft Store, to check whether you own HDRcue Pro and to buy it. Microsoft handles that under the Microsoft Privacy Statement.
privacy.contact.title: Contact
privacy.contact: For questions about this policy, open an issue on GitHub.
tour.title: Adding an app, step by step
tour.pick: Open now lists the apps and games that are running. Pick Space Arena.
tour.hdr: The main display is already picked. Set HDR to On.
tour.save: Check the summary, then select Add rule.
tour.done: Done. HDR turns on when Space Arena opens, and the display goes back when it closes.
footer.tagline: HDR for the apps you choose
